questions.q: The equation $\lambda x^{2}+4 x y+y^{2}+\lambda x+3 y+2=0$ represents a parabola, if $\lambda$ is
questions.solution:
We have the given equation as \lambda x^{2}+4 x y+y^{2}+\lambda x+3 y+2=0 On comparing this equation with $a x^{2}+2 h x y+b y^{2}+2 g x+2 f y+c=0$, we get a=\lambda, h=2, b=1, g=$\frac{\lambda}{2},$ f=$\frac{3}{2},$ c=2 Since, given equation represents a parabola \therefore h^{2}=a b \Rightarrow 4=\lambda $\cdot1 \Rightarrow \lambda=4
$

If the angular elevation of $B$ from a point $D$ due east of $C$ at a distance $2 d$ from $C$ is $r$, then $2 \tan \alpha$ can be given as
questions.solution:
By $\mathrm{m}-\mathrm{n}$ theorem at $\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{d}+2 \mathrm{ d}) \cot \beta=\mathrm{d} \cot \gamma-2 \mathrm{ d} \cot \left(90^{{}^{\circ}}+\alpha\right)
\begin{array}{l}3 d \cot \beta=$ d \cot $\gamma+2 d \tan \alpha\\ \Rightarrow 3 \cot \beta=\cot \gamma+2 \tan \alpha\\ \therefore 2 \tan \alpha=3 \cot \beta-\cot \gamma \end{array}$

questions.q: The angle of depressions of the top and the foot of a chimney as seen from the top of a second chimney, which is $150 \mathrm{ m}$ high and standing on the same level as the first are $\theta$ and $\phi$ respectively, then the distance between their tops when $\tan \theta=\frac{4}{3}$ and $\tan \phi=\frac{5}{2}$ is
questions.solution:
Given : $\tan \theta=\frac{4}{3}$ and $\tan \phi=\frac{5}{2}$
$\operatorname{In} \Delta \mathrm{ABE}\tan \phi=\frac{150}{\mathrm{ d}}\Rightarrow \mathrm{d}=150 \cot \phi=150 \times \frac{2}{5}=60 \mathrm{ m}$ In $\triangle \mathrm{DCE}\tan \theta=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{d}}\Rightarrow \frac{4}{3}=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{d}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{h}=\frac{4}{3} \times 60 \Rightarrow \mathrm{h}=80 \mathrm{ m}$ Now in $\Delta \mathrm{DCE}\mathrm{DE}^{2}=\mathrm{DC}^{2}+\mathrm{CE}^{2}\Rightarrow \mathrmx^{2}=60^{2}+80^{2}=10000\Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=100 \mathrm{ m}$

questions.q: \(A \operatorname{rod~} $\mathrm{AB~}$13 $\mathrm{ft}$\) long moves with its ends \($\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}$\) on two perpendicular lines \($\mathrm{OX}$\) and \($\mathrm{OY}$\) respectively. If the end \($\mathrm{A}$\) is \(12 $\mathrm{ft}$\) from \($\mathrm{O}$\) and is slipping away at \(2 $\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{ft}$/ $\mathrm{sec}$\). then the end \(B\) is moving at
questions.solution:
At time t, let \($\mathrm{OA}=\mathrm{x}$\) and \($\mathrm{OB}=\mathrm{y}$\). Then \($\frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{dt}}=$2 $\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{ft}$/ $\mathrm{sec}$\).
and we have to find \($\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dt}}$\). From right angled \(\triangle $\mathrm{AOB}$\), we have \($\mathrm{AB}^$2=$\mathrm{OA}^$2+$\mathrm{OB}^$2\) \(13^2=$\mathrm{x}^$2+$\mathrm{y}^$2\) ...(1) Differentiating with respect to \(t\), we get \(\therefore $\mathrm{x} \frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{dt}}+\mathrm{y} \frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dt}}=$0\) ...(2) When \($\mathrm{OA}=$12\), i.e. \($\mathrm{x}=$12\) then from (1), \(13^2=12^2+y²\) or \($\mathrm{y}=\sqrt{13^2-12^2}=$5\). Putting the values of \(y\) and \($\frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{dt}}$\) in (2), we get \(12 $\times \frac{5}{2}+$5 $\times \frac{d y}{d t}=$0\) or \(30+5 $\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dt}}=$0 ; \quad \therefore $\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dt}}=-$6 $\mathrm{ft}$/ $\mathrm{sec}$\). Hence the end B is moving at the rate of \(6 $\mathrm{ft}$/ $\mathrm{sec}$\). The negative sign shows the downward tendency of B i.e. y decreases when \(t\) increases)

questions.q: If $\mathrm{H}$ is the harmonic mean between $\mathrm{P}$ and $\mathrm{Q}$, then the value of $\frac{\mathrm{H}}{\mathrm{P}}+\frac{\mathrm{H}}{\mathrm{Q}}$ is
questions.solution:
Given : $\mathrm{H}$ is the harmonic mean between $\mathrm{P} \& \mathrm{Q}\begin{array}{l}
\therefore \mathrm{H}=\frac{2 \mathrm{PQ}}{\mathrm{P}+\mathrm{Q}} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{\mathrm{H}}=\frac{\mathrm{P}+\mathrm{Q}}{2 \mathrm{PQ}} \\
\Rightarrow \frac{2}{\mathrm{H}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{Q}}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{P}} \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{H}}{\mathrm{P}}+\frac{\mathrm{H}}{\mathrm{Q}}=2
\end{array}$
